voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: The Atlantic, eighteen seventy-two. The Mary Celeste was found drifting, empty. But the Marie Celeste most people know comes from a young Arthur Conan Doyle.
In eighteen eighty-four, before Sherlock Holmes, his story ran unsigned, told as a survivor's statement.
In it, her boats were still aboard. Even the American consul at Gibraltar asked if it was true.
In fact, her only boat was gone. Her cargo was nearly untouched. There was food and water for six months.
The story was invented. The empty ship was real. The ten aboard were never found.
